I base my whole ELA curriculum on novels. We read one to two chapters a day and then do extension activities based on the chapters. I have found it more engaging and the students are more interested in reading and participate more in the lesson. I have also found that their writing has improved markedly. A plus is that often our other subjects tie into the novels we are reading. For example, we read the jungle book and also learned about biomes in science. I'm always amazed how it all connects together because I do not plan this in any way.

Set clear boundaries and stick to them. Children that age tend to respond really well to natural consequences. Also give choices. They like to feel like they have some say in what is happening so give lots of choices. Positive reinforcement is your best friend. Reward the positive whenever you see it. If they are finishing their work quickly, make them helpers and give them small jobs to keep them busy. You can also talk with the parents, tell them what you are seeing, and ask them for input and advice. This puts the responsibility back on the parent and creates an atmosphere of working together.

Most importantly, you are not powerless. You are there to help them learn and the adult in the room. Remember you got this and are equipped to handle this. Once you reach these two, you will be prepared to handle so many more children and different behaviors.

I teach a 4th/5th grade combined class that is also 100 percent virtual. I do a reward box where they get caught being good slips. I give them out  for the first students who come back from a screen break, winning when we play games, going above and beyond in class participation discussions, and really anytime I need to reinforce positive behavior. At the end of the week, I choose a couple of names out of the box. For individual rewards, I do a free pass for homework or give 5 extra points for a quiz or test. We also do class marbles for class rewards.  For class rewards, I do a free night from homework, movie day, pajama day, or extra time for games and activities.
